result.title: CaMeWM: A Causal Medical World Model for Generative Tumor Evolution and Treatment Planning
result.summary: Treatment planning is intrinsically counterfactual: clinicians must compare how a patient's tumor and survival would evolve under competing regimens, whereas a retrospective cohort records only the regimen received and one follow-up scan. A treatment-conditioned generator trained on such data can therefore reproduce historical treatment allocation rather than simulate the interventional disease dynamics needed to rank regimens. We introduce \textbf{CaMeWM}, a causal medical world model for supported post-TACE tumor evolution and treatment planning. CaMeWM implements one intervention-to-decision loop rather than three independent prediction tasks: it first admits a queried regimen only for clinically comparable histories with empirical treatment support; it then generates a distribution of lesion-local follow-up worlds through an action-conditioned response descriptor, deterministic anchor, and residual 3D diffusion transition; and it finally maps sampled worlds to restricted mean survival time (RMST) with a response-Cox utility model. Under pre-treatment adjustment and positivity, this loop estimates a prespecified, support-restricted g-formula target; all selection and nuisance estimation are fold-local, and the induced policy is evaluated by cross-fitted, censoring-adjusted doubly robust estimation. Across 79 paired out-of-fold episodes, CaMeWM achieves 0.618 SSIM and 0.528 change-map SSIM for follow-up CT transition, while its generated-world survival pathway attains a 0.615 C-index; factual-only AIPW estimates a 9.60-week RMST gain (95\% CI 0.61--18.13) for the frozen policy. CaMeWM provides an inspectable basis for retrospective, support-restricted treatment planning.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 CaMeWM 因果医学世界模型：以治疗条件化的响应描述、确定性锚点与残差 3D 扩散转移生成 TACE 术后病灶随访世界，再经响应-Cox 效用模型映射到 RMST，用于支持域受限的治疗方案比较。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「仅在经验治疗支持充分时才允许生成反事实状态」及动作条件化状态转移、状态到决策的回路，可能与 LVR 中潜状态更新的证据支持筛选与停止/弃权判断有概念联系，可供核查；但论文不涉及语言推理或 latent reasoning 验证。
